hints: Since $100 > 25$, conclude that $T(11, 5)$ lies outside the circle.
walkthrough:
An external point is farther from the centre than the radius.
Extract centre $C(3, -1)$ and calculate the squared distance $TC^2$:
$$TC^2 = (11 - 3)^2 + (5 - (-1))^2 = 8^2 + 6^2 = 64 + 36 = 100$$

Compare $TC^2$ with $r^2 = 25$:
$$100 > 25 \implies TC > r$$
$$\text{Therefore, } T(11, 5) \text{ lies strictly outside the circle } C.$$

hints: The triangle $\triangle TCA$ has right angle at $A$ (radius perpendicular to tangent).
walkthrough:
An external point is farther from the centre than the radius.
Apply Pythagoras in right-angled triangle $\triangle TCA$ with hypotenuse $TC$:
$$TC^2 = CA^2 + TA^2$$
$$100 = 25 + TA^2 \implies TA^2 = 75$$
